title: Telemetry-first mini-launch checklist for staggered model-variant onboarding
creator: Alex Chen
summary: Run a small, telemetry-led launch for a new model variant into the catalog with staggered canary cohorts. Prioritize fast feedback loops, minimal documentation to unblock integrators, and clear rollback criteria tied to micro-metrics.
objectives: Validate latency and per-token cost for the new variant under production traffic samples
Detect regressions in generation quality vs baseline on core benchmark sets
Ensure minimal docs and sample SDK snippets are published so early adopters can integrate
Establish automated alerts and a short remediation runbook for the first 72 hours
success_metrics: Latency P95 within 10% of baseline model across 95th percentile traffic
Token cost per 1k within acceptable delta (<= +15%)
Quality regression rate on core prompt suite < 3% compared to pinned baseline
No Sev2+ incidents attributable to model behavior during canary window
benchmarks: Core suite: 200 prompts across generation and chat contexts (benchmarks/storage path: drive/redwood/benchmarks/2026/variant-minilaunch)
KV cache hit/miss rate under simulated conversational traffic
End-to-end wall clock for streaming responses (90th percentile targets)
prelaunch_tasks: Run final 1k-sample perf sweep on staging with real traffic replay (ENG)
Create minimal docs: quickstart, code snippet for SDK, opt-in toggle instructions (PM + DX)
Prepare release notes draft and feature TL;DR (PM)
Register canary cohorts and route rules in runtime config (ENG)
Configure monitoring dashboards and automated alerts (SRE + ENG)
Verify keys/quotas and rate limits for early adopters (Ops)
Legal/PD review completed for model license and data handling (Legal)
Prepare short internal playbook for escalation and rollback (PM + SRE)
rollout_steps: Step 0: Feature gate closed. Dry-run internal traffic only for 3 hours.
Step 1: Canary cohort A (1% of production traffic) for 6 hours; observe micro-metrics.
Step 2: If stable, escalate to cohort B (5% of traffic) for 12 hours with extended evals.
Step 3: Cohort C (25% traffic) for 24 hours; open signups to a small set of beta customers.
Step 4: Full catalog listing with clear variant tags if all prior cohorts pass criteria.
Step 5: Post-launch evaluation window: 7 days of extended monitoring and benchmark sweeps.
canary_criteria: No SLO breach or Sev2+ incidents caused by the variant during cohort window
Latency P95 delta <= +10% vs baseline across monitored endpoints
Quality regression < 3% on core prompt suite with human-in-the-loop checks for any flagged prompts
Errors per 1k requests <= baseline + 1.5x for transient spikes only
rollback_triggers: SLO violation sustained for >= 15 minutes at P95 or P99 and not explained by infra changes
Quality regression spike > 5% on core prompts confirmed by evaluation harness
Unusual hallucination patterns flagged by monitoring (content-safety alerts) with >3 distinct customers reporting
Increase in error-rate to >= 2x baseline for more than 10 minutes
docs_and_assets: Quickstart: 6-line SDK snippet showing model selection and streaming (DX draft link)
Minimal API reference for new variant (auto-generated + PM edits)
Known limitations section: tokenization differences, recommended max seq len
Benchmarks summary card (visual) for catalog listing
Support playbook and FAQ for early adopters
release_notes_template: TL;DR: New model variant added to catalog offering lower cost for short-form generation. Breaking changes: none. Known issues: edge-case coherence at >1024 tokens. Technical notes: quantization configuration and suggested batching knobs. Migration: opt-in via modelVariant param. Contact: pm+models@redwood.ai
communications: Internal: Slack #product-models @here announcement at cohort B gate with monitoring snapshot link
Internal: Postmortem channel and zoom bridge prepared for launch day
External: Blog micro-post + short benchmark highlights after cohort C
External: Release notes published in docs site and attached to catalog entry
Sales: One-pager for SDRs describing ideal early adopter use cases and cost delta
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Latency regression under long-sequence tails. Mitigation: cap initial seq_len to 1024 for canary cohorts and run extended kernel sweep.
Risk: Unexpected generation quality regressions on niche prompts. Mitigation: run small human-review panel on flagged prompts and maintain canary rollback window.
Risk: Early adopters confused by variant naming. Mitigation: concise docs, sample code, and product listing badges.
Risk: Monitoring gaps for streaming edge cases. Mitigation: add stream-level instrumentation in runtime and a synthetic stream test during Step 0.
QA_checklist: End-to-end integration test for SDK sample snippet passes
Automated benchmark harness run completes with pass/fail artifact uploaded
Chaos/forced error test on staging routing rules to ensure robust fallback
Permission checks: keys and quotas validated for early adopter orgs
launch_day_script: T-60m: Final monitoring health check and Slack prep message
T-0: Open cohort A routing and post initial snapshot to slack
+1h: Collect automated benchmark and perf data; brief check-in with ENG/SRE
Gate decision: proceed to cohort B if canary_criteria pass; otherwise, rollback per runbook
If rollback: announce to internal channels and trigger postmortem template
post_launch_monitoring: Automated evaluation sweep at 6h, 12h, 24h, and daily for 7 days
Customer support triage queue prioritized for early adopters
Daily status snapshot to execs during first 72 hours
Collect qualitative feedback from beta customers and map to bugs/feature requests
followups: Collect final metric pack and decide promotion date for full listing
Iterate on docs to cover integration edge-cases discovered in canaries
Schedule retro within 10 days and publish lessons learned
If stable, propose next experiment: quantized variant or different kernel profile
